title: OISST trend gaps remain positive across 200 HadSST4 bias cases in the east Pacific and at 50-60 S in 1982-2022
abstract: We tested whether reference bias adjustments cause the positive OISST v2.1 minus HadSST4 trend gap. We matched median, unadjusted and all 200 HadSST.4.2.0.0 members to the same five-degree cells and months. HadSST4 adjustments add 0.0434 C per decade in the east equatorial Pacific and 0.0361 at 50-60 S in 1982-2022. They reduce the OISST gaps from 0.0678 to 0.0245 and from 0.0948 to 0.0588 C per decade. The bias-ensemble 95 percent gap ranges are 0.0164 to 0.0309 and 0.0535 to 0.0659. All 200 members retain positive gaps in both regions. The bias and residual-block mixture ranges are 0.0037 to 0.0444 and 0.0366 to 0.0817 C per decade. A fit with cell and calendar-month offsets gives similar positive gaps. Reference adjustments therefore do not create the median gap, but ensemble and time-series uncertainty must be kept separate. Unadjusted SST is a diagnostic, not climate truth. Shared source data, sparse coverage, missing measurement-error propagation and unrepresented structural bias limit inference. No step correction or atmospheric response is fitted.

display.caption: Matched 1982-2022 trend gaps, reference adjustment and bias-ensemble uncertainty. See README for the limited error model.
